meta.title: Hypercare: Ends on Proof, Not a Calendar Date

views.label: Tightened thresholds, elevated staffing
views.note: Job success, cost, data freshness, and ticket volume all watched daily against the source baseline.

views.label: Severity defined before the first incident
views.note: P1 pages immediately; P3 is tracked and reviewed in the daily hypercare sync.

views.label: An explicit gate, agreed before cutover
views.note: N consecutive clean SLA days plus a full business cycle -- without a gate, hypercare quietly becomes permanent.

cards.title: What changes during hypercare
items: On-call moves to elevated staffing, often a dedicated war-room or Slack channel
Change control freezes on unrelated work to reduce noise while diagnosing issues
Source stays fully running and reachable for rollback -- not yet decommissioned
A resolved incident returns to elevated monitoring, not to normal operations -- the clean-window count resets

cards.title: Severity is agreed before the first incident, not during it
items: P1: migration-caused outage or data-correctness issue -- page immediately, resolve within hours
P2: degradation with a workaround -- same-day resolution
P3: cosmetic, no workaround needed -- tracked in the daily sync

cards.title: The exit gate is explicit, or hypercare never ends
items: Define the gate before cutover: N consecutive clean SLA days plus one full business cycle
Decommission source last -- 'looks successful on day one' and 'proven stable' are different claims
